nodes.label: Build and quick start
nodes.rationale: Recommends --llm=off as the first run because it needs no API keys and is the fastest sanity check. Java 21 is a hard requirement - the main class is compiled to class-file version 65.0 and anything older fails with UnsupportedClassVersionError - so JAVA_HOME guidance appears before any build command.

nodes.label: Environment Variables section
nodes.rationale: Added to close AUDIT C1: variables read directly by the code and not exposed as CLI flags, grouped by purpose with default and actual effect. CRYSLDOC_COMPILE_CHECK carries an explicit warning that the gate is the only thing preventing broken examples from reaching the documentation, so it should be turned off deliberately or not at all.

nodes.label: Timeout layering rule
nodes.rationale: The two timeout layers must stay ordered: the Python client's worst case, (1 + LLM_MAX_RETRIES) x LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, has to fit inside the Java-side ceiling for the same call, or Java kills the sidecar mid-retry and the work is lost rather than retried. With the shipped llm/.env values that is 360 s against a 480 s explanation ceiling.

nodes.label: UPB AI-Gateway backend setup
nodes.rationale: GATEWAY_EMB_MODEL is required for secure example generation because there is no working embedding fallback for the gateway; chat model and base URL do have built-in UPB defaults. Gateway chat and embedding requests are throttled client-side by a shared cross-process limiter defaulting to 10 RPM, and no fallback to OpenAI is performed in gateway mode.

nodes.label: First-time run required for LLM features
nodes.rationale: A documented one-time preprocessing pass compensating for a code-level coupling: sanitized JSON generation is tied to the explanation flow in DocSettings, so it must run with --llm=on even though the artifacts it produces are consumed by the example writers. Explanation calls failing for lack of API keys during this pass is expected.

nodes.label: Code cache cleanup helper
nodes.rationale: delete_disabled_code_cache_files.py pre-dates placeholder-aware invalidation and is no longer needed to un-poison a cache; it remains useful for forcing clean regeneration after a model or backend change, which the filename-only cache key cannot detect.
